# How to Pay Employees on Time Every Month: A Small Business Owner’s Checklist for India (2026)


October 13, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-to-pay-employees-on-time-every-month-a-small-business-owners-checklist-for-india-2026/#respond)


Every employee remembers the day their salary was late. Not by a week. Not by a month. Even a single day of delay can shake their trust in your business.


For small business owners in India, paying employees on time is not just about keeping people happy. It is a legal requirement under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936. Missing the deadline can attract fines, penalties, and even imprisonment for repeat offenders.


Yet salary delays remain one of the most common problems faced by Indian SMEs. The reasons are familiar: cash flow gaps, manual payroll errors, forgotten compliance deadlines, and last minute attendance disputes. The good news? Most of these problems are preventable with the right system and a simple monthly checklist.


This guide gives you a complete, step by step monthly payroll checklist designed specifically for Indian small businesses. Follow it every month, and you will never miss a salary date again.


## Why Paying Employees on Time Actually Matters


Before diving into the checklist, let us understand what is really at stake when salaries get delayed.


### The Legal Reality


The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 sets clear deadlines for salary payment in India:


Business Size Salary Payment Deadline


Less than 1,000 employees By the 7th of the following month


1,000 or more employees By the 10th of the following month


Terminated or resigned employees Within 2 working days of last day


Most small businesses in India have fewer than 1,000 employees, which means your salary must reach every employee’s bank account by the 7th of every month. No exceptions.


### Penalties Under the Payment of Wages Act (Section 20)


Violation Penalty


First offence (delayed wages or unauthorized deduction) Fine of ₹1,500 to ₹7,500


Repeat offence 1 to 6 months imprisonment plus fine of ₹3,750 to ₹22,500


Obstructing a labour inspector Up to 6 months imprisonment, fine up to ₹7,500, or both


Under Code on Wages, 2019 (when notified) Fine up to ₹50,000


### The Business Impact Beyond Legal Penalties


Impact Area What Happens When Salary Is Delayed


Employee trust Drops immediately, even with a one day delay


Attrition Employees start looking for other jobs within weeks


Productivity Work output declines when employees are worried about finances


Employer branding Word spreads fast, making future hiring harder


Team morale Remaining employees lose confidence in management


Referral hiring Stops completely when current employees are unhappy


According to the Aon India Salary Increase Survey 2026, average attrition in Indian companies stands at around 13.6%. Salary delays accelerate this number significantly for small businesses that cannot afford to lose trained staff.

## The Complete Monthly Payroll Checklist (Day by Day)


Here is your exact, day by day checklist to ensure salaries go out on time every single month.


### Phase 1: Data Collection (1st to 3rd of Every Month)


This is where most payroll delays actually begin. If attendance data, leave records, and variable pay inputs are not finalized early, everything else gets pushed back.


#### Day 1 Checklist


Task Details Who Is Responsible


Lock previous month’s attendance Finalize total present days, half days, absences HR or business owner


Collect overtime records Document all approved overtime hours with supervisor sign off Department heads


Verify leave balances Cross check leave applications with actual attendance HR


Gather variable pay inputs Incentives, commissions, bonus amounts, deductions for advances Accounts or HR


#### Day 2 Checklist


Task Details Who Is Responsible


Confirm new joiners Add employees who joined last month to payroll HR


Process exits Calculate full and final for employees who left HR and Accounts


Update salary revisions Apply any increments or restructuring effective this month HR


Verify bank details Confirm account numbers for new employees and any changes HR


#### Day 3 Checklist


Task Details Who Is Responsible


Send data to accounts/payroll Share finalized attendance and variable inputs HR to Accounts


Flag exceptions Highlight any disputes, pending approvals, or unclear cases HR


Get management approval Owner or manager sign off on variable pay and exceptions Business owner


**Pro Tip:** If you are using[SalaryBox for attendance tracking](https://salarybox.in/attendance-management-system) , your attendance data is already locked automatically at month end. No manual collection needed.


### Phase 2: Payroll Calculation (3rd to 4th of Every Month)


This is the calculation phase where gross salary, deductions, and net pay are computed.


#### Payroll Calculation Checklist


Step What to Calculate Formula or Rule


1 Gross salary for the month (Monthly CTC components) adjusted for attendance


2 Loss of Pay (LOP) deduction (Gross salary / Total working days) × Absent days


3 PF employee contribution 12% of Basic + DA (capped at ₹15,000 basic)


4 ESI employee contribution 0.75% of gross salary (if gross ≤ ₹21,000)


5 Professional Tax As per state slab


6 TDS on salary Based on projected annual income and tax regime


7 Other deductions Loan recovery, advance adjustment, salary advance


8 Net salary (take home) Gross salary minus all deductions


#### Employer Cost Calculation (Separate from Employee Salary)


Component Rate Paid By


PF employer contribution 12% of Basic + DA (includes 8.33% pension, 3.67% PF) Employer


ESI employer contribution 3.25% of gross salary (if gross ≤ ₹21,000) Employer


EDLI (Employee Deposit Linked Insurance) 0.50% of Basic + DA Employer


PF admin charges 0.50% of Basic + DA Employer


For a complete breakdown of all employment costs beyond salary, read our guide on[the total cost of hiring an employee in India](https://salarybox.in/blog/cost-of-hiring-employee-india-2026-complete-breakdown/) .


### Phase 3: Verification and Approval (4th to 5th of Every Month)


Never process salary without a verification step. This single habit prevents 90% of payroll errors.


#### Verification Checklist


Check What to Verify Red Flag If


Headcount match Total employees on payroll vs active employee list Numbers do not match (ghost employees or missed additions)


Salary comparison This month’s total payout vs last month’s Variance exceeds 5% without a known reason


New joiner proration Salary calculated for actual days worked, not full month New joiner getting full month salary for partial attendance


Exit settlement Full and final includes all pending leaves, gratuity, notice pay F&F amount is exactly equal to monthly salary (likely not calculated properly)


Statutory deductions PF, ESI, PT, TDS amounts match expected calculations Deduction amounts are zero or unchanged despite salary changes


Bank details Account numbers verified for new employees Transfer to wrong account is almost impossible to reverse quickly


#### Approval Workflow


Step Action Timeline


1 Payroll team generates salary sheet By end of Day 4


2 HR head or business owner reviews and approves By noon on Day 5


3 Final salary file sent to bank or payment processor By end of Day 5


### Phase 4: Salary Disbursement (5th to 7th of Every Month)


This is the actual payment phase. Your goal is to have salaries credited by the 7th at the latest.


#### Salary Payment Checklist


Task Details Deadline


Generate bank transfer file NEFT/IMPS/UPI bulk payment file with employee details Day 5


Initiate bank transfer Upload file to corporate banking portal or payment system Day 5 or 6


Verify credits Confirm all transfers are successful, identify bounced payments Day 6 or 7


Resolve failures Re-initiate failed transfers with corrected bank details Same day


Send salary notifications Inform employees that salary has been credited Day 7


#### Salary Payment Modes Available in India


Payment Mode Processing Time Best For


NEFT (National Electronic Fund Transfer) Same day (hourly batches) Standard salary transfers


IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) Instant Urgent or small payments


UPI (Unified Payments Interface) Instant Small teams, quick transfers


RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement) Instant (for amounts above ₹2 lakh) Large salary payments


Cheque 2 to 3 working days for clearing Not recommended for regular salary


Cash Immediate Only for exceptional cases, must be documented


**Important:** The Payment of Wages Act allows digital payment modes. Since 2017, many states require bank transfer for establishments above certain employee counts. Cash payments must be documented with signed receipts.

### Phase 5: Statutory Compliance (7th to 15th of Every Month)


After paying salaries, you have a narrow window to deposit statutory contributions. Miss these, and you face interest charges and penalties on top of the principal amount.


#### Statutory Payment Checklist

This phase is about maintaining records that protect your business during inspections and audits.


#### Documentation Checklist


Document What It Contains Retention Period

Bank transfer proof NEFT/IMPS confirmation for all salary payments 3 years minimum

## The 5 Most Common Reasons Small Businesses Delay Salary (and How to Fix Each One)


Understanding why delays happen is the first step toward preventing them.


### Reason 1: Cash Flow Gaps


**The Problem:** Revenue collection does not align with salary dates. Many small businesses receive payments from clients on the 15th or 20th, but salaries are due by the 7th.


**The Fix:**


Strategy How It Works


Maintain a salary reserve fund Keep 1.5 months of payroll in a separate bank account


Negotiate client payment terms Request payment by the 25th of the previous month


Use invoice factoring Convert outstanding invoices to immediate cash through NBFC services


Stagger large expenses Avoid scheduling rent, vendor payments, and EMIs in the first week


### Reason 2: Attendance Data Delays


**The Problem:** Attendance records are not finalized until the 5th or 6th, leaving no time for payroll calculation.


**The Fix:**


Strategy How It Works


Automate attendance tracking Use an[attendance management system](https://salarybox.in/attendance-management-system) with GPS or biometric


Set attendance lock deadline Auto lock attendance on the 1st of every month


Train managers Make attendance approval a daily habit, not a monthly task


### Reason 3: Manual Payroll Errors


**The Problem:** Calculating salary manually in Excel leads to formula errors, missed deductions, and rework.


**The Fix:**


Manual Process Time Taken Error Rate Automated Alternative


Attendance compilation 2 to 3 days 15 to 20% discrepancy rate Auto sync from attendance app


Salary calculation 1 to 2 days 5 to 10% error rate One click payroll processing


PF/ESI computation Half a day Frequent cap miscalculations Auto calculated based on rules


Payslip generation 1 day Formatting errors Instant digital payslips


Bank file creation Half a day Account number typos Auto generated from employee database


**Total time saved with automation: 5 to 7 working days per month**


Read our detailed comparison of[SalaryBox vs Excel for payroll management](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-excel-payroll-management/) .


### Reason 4: Compliance Confusion


**The Problem:** Business owners do not know which employees need PF deduction, which are eligible for ESI, or how much Professional Tax to deduct for each state.


**The Fix:**


Confusion Quick Rule


Who needs PF? All employees in establishments with 20+ employees (voluntary for smaller)


Who needs ESI? Employees earning gross salary ≤ ₹21,000 in establishments with 10+ employees


How much TDS? Based on employee’s chosen tax regime and projected annual income


Professional Tax? Depends on your state. Not applicable in Delhi, UP, Rajasthan


For a complete understanding of these thresholds, read our[guide to minimum employees for PF, ESI, gratuity, and bonus](https://salarybox.in/blog/minimum-employees-pf-esi-gratuity-bonus-india/) .


### Reason 5: No Fixed Payroll Calendar


**The Problem:** There is no defined schedule for who does what and by when. Payroll becomes a scramble in the last 2 days before the deadline.


**The Fix:** Adopt the day by day checklist from this guide. Print it, pin it on your office wall, and assign clear owners for each task.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### 1. What is the legal deadline for paying salary in India?


Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, employers with fewer than 1,000 employees must pay wages by the 7th of the following month. Employers with 1,000 or more employees have until the 10th. For employees who are terminated or who resign, the final settlement must be completed within 2 working days of their last working day.


### 2. What happens if an employer pays salary late in India?


Late salary payment is a violation of the Payment of Wages Act. First time offenders face a fine of ₹1,500 to ₹7,500. Repeat offenders can face imprisonment of 1 to 6 months along with a fine of ₹3,750 to ₹22,500. Additionally, employees can file complaints with the Labour Commissioner, and the employer may face legal proceedings.


### 3. Can salary be paid in cash in India?


Yes, salary can be paid in cash under the Payment of Wages Act, but it is strongly discouraged. The Income Tax Act restricts cash payments above ₹10,000 per day (Section 269ST). Many states require bank transfer for establishments above certain employee counts. Cash payments must be documented with signed receipts from employees.


### 4. What is the due date for PF payment every month?


The employer must deposit PF contributions (both employer and employee share) by the 15th of the following month through the ECR (Electronic Challan cum Return) on the EPFO Unified Portal. For example, PF for September salaries must be paid by October 15th.


### 5. What is the penalty for late PF deposit?


Late PF payment attracts 12% annual interest under Section 7Q of the EPF Act. Additionally, damages of 1% per month are levied under Section 14B (revised post June 15, 2024). In severe cases, the EPFO can initiate criminal prosecution under Section 14 with fines up to ₹5,000 and imprisonment up to 1 year. Read more in our detailed guide on[PF and ESI non registration penalties](https://salarybox.in/blog/what-happens-if-you-dont-register-for-pf-or-esi-india/) .


### 6. How can a small business ensure payroll is processed on time every month?


Follow a structured monthly checklist: lock attendance by the 1st, calculate payroll by the 3rd to 4th, get approval by the 5th, disburse salary by the 5th to 6th, and deposit TDS by the 7th. Using[payroll software like SalaryBox](https://salarybox.in/) automates most of these steps and reduces the entire process from 5 to 7 days to under 1 hour.


### 7. Is it mandatory to give salary slips to employees in India?


While the Payment of Wages Act does not explicitly mandate salary slips, most state Shops and Establishments Acts require employers to provide a written statement of wages showing all deductions. Under the Code on Wages, 2019 (when fully notified), salary slips become a mandatory requirement for all employers. It is a best practice to issue digital salary slips every month.


### 8. What payroll records must an employer maintain in India?


Employers must maintain: a wage register (Form C) showing gross salary, deductions, and net pay; an attendance register; overtime records; PF and ESI payment challans; TDS deposit receipts; and individual payslips for each employee. These records must be retained for a minimum of 3 years under the Payment of Wages Act, and 7 years for tax related documents under the Income Tax Act.


## Conclusion


Paying employees on time is one of the simplest ways to build trust, reduce attrition, and stay legally compliant. Yet it remains a challenge for thousands of Indian small businesses every month.


The fix is not complicated. It comes down to having a clear monthly schedule, locking attendance early, automating calculations, and staying on top of compliance deadlines. This checklist gives you everything you need to make payroll predictable instead of stressful.


Start by adopting just the first two phases: data collection and payroll calculation. Once those are running smoothly, the rest will follow naturally.
